name: the beach
title: A Grey Beach
description: Wet sand, broken shells, a line of wrack. The wind never quite stops.
Wet sand and broken shells, and a line of wrack. The wind does not stop.
Grey sand, grey sea, a line of wrack. The wind is always here.
_map: position on the route map (grid cells); the camp (travelHours 0) has a path to every place
_arrive: what you see each time you come back: every line whose 'when' holds, in order

text: Back on the sand. The wind finds you at once.
The sand again, and the wind with it.
You come out onto the beach. The wind is waiting.
The beach again: wet sand, a line of wrack.
The beach: the same wet sand, the same wrack.
Wet sand underfoot again. Wrack along the tide line.
The beach in the dark. Only the surf, and a pale line of foam.
In the dark the beach is only sound: the surf, the wind.
Night on the beach. The foam glows faintly at the water's edge.
Smoke rises from the ring of rocks.
A thread of smoke above the ring of rocks.
The fire is still alive in the rocks.
The ring of rocks waits, cold.
The ring of rocks, and cold ash inside it.
No smoke from the rocks. The fire is out.
Shells on the stone under the cliff.
The shells still cling under the cliff.
Under the cliff, the shells wait for the tide.
Fish flash in the shallows.
Something silver turns in the shallows.
The fish are still in the shallows.

explore.name: look around
explore._explore: look around: a pop-up with what you see (view lines whose 'when' holds) and the landmarks not explored yet; no time passes until you pick one

text: Grey sand runs both ways until it bends out of sight. Wrack and broken shells mark the tide line.
The beach stretches both ways, grey and empty. Wrack marks the tide line.
Sand, wrack and broken shells, as far as you can see.

view.text: Behind the dunes, a dark line of trees.
At the far end of the beach, a ring of dark rocks.
At the far end, the ring of rocks, out of the wind.
Past the rocks, a low cliff drops into the surf.
Under the cliff, shells on the wet stone.
The cliff above them looks climbable.
Beyond the cliff, to the west, the meadows.

nothingLeft: There is nothing here you have not seen.

landmarks.label: the dunes
text: You climb the dunes. From the top the beach runs both ways until it bends out of sight. Behind them the trees begin. A forest, close and hard to miss.
Up the soft sand of the dunes. On the other side, trunks and shade: a forest, close enough to walk to.
From the crest of the dunes you see the island's edge give way to trees. A forest, an hour's walk at most.

landmarks.label: the ring of rocks
text: At the far end of the beach, a ring of rocks breaks the sea wind. You could light a fire here, if you find some wood.
At the end of the beach, rocks stand in a ring, out of the wind. A fire would keep here, with some wood.
A ring of rocks at the far end of the sand. The wind can't reach inside. A good place for a fire, if you had wood.

landmarks.label: the low cliff
text: Past the rocks, a low cliff drops into the surf. Shells cling to the wet stone below it. You could pick them and eat them as they are. Cooked, they would go further.
Beyond the rocks, a low cliff meets the sea. Shells crowd the wet stone at its foot. You could eat them raw, or cook them for more.
Under a low cliff past the rocks, shells cover the wet stone. Food, of a kind: raw, or better cooked.

landmarks.label: the shallows
text: In the shallows, a school of small fish turns and flashes. Too quick for bare hands. With a sharp stick you might spear one.
Small fish dart in the shallows, a whole school of them. Your hands are too slow. A spear might do it.
Silver flashes in the shallow water: fish, many of them. Too fast to grab. A sharp stick could reach them.

landmarks.label: climb the cliff
text: You climb the cliff, handhold by handhold. From the top the land opens out to the west: long grass in waves, bushes, a line of willows. Meadows, an hour's walk away.
Up the cliff, slowly, the wind pulling at you. At the top you see what the cliff was hiding: meadows to the west, wide and green, an hour away.
The climb is short but steep. From the top, inland to the west, grass rolls away under the wind: meadows, maybe an hour's walk.

activities.name: light fire
log: A match flares. A curl of smoke, then the kindling catches. The fire takes.
You shield a match in your hands. The flame jumps to the kindling.
One match, struck carefully. The fire is lit.

activities.name: light fire
activities._note: without matches: friction, 2 h, catches 2 times in 3; the wood is only used when it catches
log: You twist a dry stick against a branch, again and again, until your palms burn.
No matches. You spin a stick between your hands until your arms ache.
You rub wood on wood, slow and stubborn, blowing on every wisp of smoke.

text: A glow, a breath, and at last a flame. The fire takes.
The wisp of smoke becomes an ember, then a flame.
Finally, a flame. You feed it, careful as with a newborn.
Smoke, but no flame. The wood will do for another try.
The ember dies before it catches. You keep the wood.
Your hands give out first. No fire, not yet.

activities.name: stoke fire
log: The fire crackles.
The flames climb higher.
You feed the fire. It answers.
Sparks climb into the dark.
Sparks drift up on the wind.
The new wood catches with a hiss.

activities.name: collect shells
log: You prise shells off the wet stone. The surf soaks your legs.
You work the shells loose with your fingers. The surf breaks over your knees.
Shell by shell, off the wet stone. Your hands go numb.
A handful of shells, cold and heavy.
A pocketful of shells, cold and wet.
Shells, heavy and dripping.

activities.name: pick up stones
log: Under the cliff, stones of every size. You pick the hardest.
You choose stones from the foot of the cliff, flat and heavy.
You gather stones where the cliff has crumbled.
activities._note: stones lie under the cliff: shown once you need them (a rock knife without the knife, the axe, the hoe, the weir)

activities.name: catch fish

text: Two fish, flapping on the sand.
Two fish, one on each strike.
Two fish thrash on the sand.
One fish. It will do.
One fish, wriggling on the point.
A single fish. Enough for now.
Nothing. The fish are quicker than you.
Nothing. They scatter every time.
The water swirls. The spear comes up empty.

log: You wade into the shallows, spear raised.
You stand knee-deep in the cold water and wait.
Spear ready, you wade out slowly.

activities.name: sleep
activities.requiresText: Too cold and dark to sleep without a fire or a shelter
activities._thoughts: before sleeping: how tired you are (energy, same bands as the bar), then up to 3 things you remember from today, most memorable first

text: You drop by the fire, too exhausted to feel the cold sand.
You fall down by the fire. You can't keep your eyes open.
Your legs give way by the fire. Too tired to care.
You curl up by the fire. Every muscle aches.
You lie down by the fire. Everything hurts.
You curl up by the warmth, aching all over.
You curl up by the fire, tired in a slow, heavy way.
You stretch out by the fire. A slow tiredness comes over you.
You lie by the fire, heavy and tired.
You lie by the fire, not really tired. Sleep is slow to come.
You lie by the fire and stare at the sky. Sleep takes its time.
You are not tired. You lie by the fire and wait for sleep.

intro: The day comes back to you in pieces.
Pieces of the day drift back.
You think back over the day.
Lying still, you go over the day.
In the quiet, the day replays.
Before sleep, the day returns to you.

text: The cold sea. Waking alone on the sand.
The shock of waking on the beach, alone.
Salt, cold, and no ship on the horizon.
Carving the spear with the knife, shaving by shaving.
The knife turning a branch into a spear.
The spear you carved, its point sharp under your thumb.
Hacking at a branch with the rock knife until it had a point.
The blunt rock knife, and the spear it made, slowly.
A spear made with a blade of stone.
Grinding a stone into a blade, for hours.
Stone on stone, until it had an edge.
The rock knife, and how long it took.
Fish flashing in the shallows, just out of reach.
Silver fish in the shallows, too quick to catch.
The fish in the shallows, so close.
Building the shelter, log by log.
The shelter against the rocks, and how still it is inside.
The wind breaking on the logs you raised.
The first harvest from the field.
Breaking the corn off the stalks.
Arms full of corn.
Hacking at the wood with the axe.
The axe biting into wood.
Logs, real logs, at last.
Standing in the surf with the spear raised.
Cold water to your knees, the spear ready.
Waiting in the surf for the fish to come close.
The view from the cliff top: grass all the way inland.
The wind at the top of the cliff, and the meadows below.
Climbing the cliff, and the green land behind it.
A clear river under the willows.
The river, cold and quick over the stones.
Fish holding still in the river's slow pools.
Wading in the river with the spear raised.
The river pulling at your legs while you waited for a fish.
Fishing in the slow pools under the willows.
A match flaring in your cupped hands, then warmth.
One match, and the fire took.
The smell of a struck match, then woodsmoke.
Wood against wood until your palms burned, and at last a flame.
Hours of rubbing sticks before the fire came.
Your raw palms, and the first ember.
Cold water from a spring between mossy stones.
The spring, and how cold the water was.
Drinking from the spring until your teeth ached.
A ring of rocks, out of the wind.
The ring of rocks where the wind can't reach.
Shelter among the rocks.
The cool dark under the trees.
The forest, quiet and dim.
Tall trunks and the smell of moss.
Long grass, and the wind moving through it.
The open meadows under a wide sky.
Grass to the knee, silver in the wind.
Purple fingers from the berries.
Picking berries, thorns in your sleeves.
The sour, sweet taste of the berries.
The smell of food over the fire.
Food cooking on the hot stones.
The smell of something cooking.
Armful after armful of dry branches.
Dragging dry branches out of the forest.
Bark and twigs, scratching your arms.
Shells pried from the wet stone.
Cold fingers on wet shells.
Shells, and the surf soaking your legs.
The taste of fresh water.
Water, at last.
Cold, clean water.
Something in your stomach, at least.
Food, of a kind.
You ate. That is something.

otherwise: A day of small things. You hardly remember it.
The day blurs. Nothing stands out.
Little to remember. Sand, waiting, more sand.
thoughts._lines: most memorable first; the fire and the spear are remembered the way you did them (matches or friction, knife or rock knife)

log: Sleep takes you.
Your eyes close.
Darkness, and then nothing.
At last, sleep.
Sleep comes quickly.
You drift off.
activities._afterwards: the night itself is quiet; on waking: the time, then one line on how your body is (worst first), then the fire

text: Morning comes, grey and wet.
Grey dawn, damp and cold.
The light comes back, thin and grey.
You wake in the dark. The surf is loud.
You wake. It is still dark, and the surf roars.
Darkness still. Only the sound of the sea.
Your body is weak and shaking. The night took something from you.
You are weak. Your hands won't stop shaking.
You can barely sit up. The night was hard on you.
Hunger and thirst, both at once.
Your stomach aches and your mouth is dry.
Hungry, thirsty, both.
Your mouth is dry, your tongue thick.
Your throat is dry as sand.
Thirst wakes you before the light does.
Your stomach is a hollow ache.
Hunger, first thing.
Your belly is empty and loud.
You are stiff with cold.
The cold has got into your joints.
You wake shivering.
You feel rested.
You feel stronger.
Rested, for once.
You are still tired.
Tired still, though you slept.
The sleep did little.
The fire still smoulders in the ring of rocks.
Embers still glow in the rocks.
A little smoke still rises from the fire.
The fire is long out. Only cold ash.
Cold ash where the fire was.
The fire is gone. Not even smoke.
The fire died in the night.
Sometime in the night, the fire went out.
The fire did not last the night.
